html:
The Green Revolution in India was the shift, from the mid 1960s, to high yield wheat and rice, irrigation, fertiliser and pesticides that ended India's dependence on food aid. It started in Punjab and Haryana.

India in 1965 and 1966 was close to famine, living on grain shipped from the United States, and the memory of the Bengal famine of 1943 was fresh. Agriculture minister C. Subramaniam and the scientist M. S. Swaminathan brought in dwarf wheat bred in Mexico by Norman Borlaug, then rice varieties from the International Rice Research Institute in the Philippines. Government price guarantees and cheap power for tube wells did the rest.

  • Wheat harvests roughly doubled within a few years; see Green Revolution wheat in India.
  • By the 1970s India fed itself and built grain reserves.

The costs came later: falling water tables in Punjab, worn soils, chemical use, and gains that went mostly to farmers with land and water. The crop prices it set up lie behind the farmers' protest of 2020.
sum: The Green Revolution in India was the shift, from the mid 1960s, to high yield wheat and rice, irrigation, fertiliser and pesticides that ended India's dependence on food aid. It started in Punjab and Haryana.
